llm.summary: This skill clearly dispatches paid local errand workers through the Errand API and requires user confirmation before spending money.

dimensions.detail: Network calls, geocoding, the API key, and sending task/location details to errand.be are proportionate for a service that hires a real worker and returns photo/GPS evidence.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is a single Markdown skill requiring curl and an ERRANDAI_API_KEY; it also documents an optional remote MCP setup command, which users should treat as a persistent integration choice.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The runtime flow is scoped to coverage checks, quotes, explicit user approval, dispatch, polling, result retrieval, cancellation, and listing recent dispatches; it explicitly says not to dispatch without the user's yes to a stated total price.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill itself contains no executable files or persistence mechanism, but the optional MCP command would add a reusable remote tool configuration outside the one-off curl workflow.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The API key, external Errand service, paid dispatch flow, GPS/photo evidence, and worker-facing task details all match the stated purpose of sending a person to check or photograph a Seoul location.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable giving this skill an Errand API key and sending location/task details to errand.be and a human worker. Review the price before approving any dispatch, because confirmed dispatches escrow prepaid KRW and cannot be cancelled after a worker accepts.
llm.findings:
[E1] expected: The flagged external transmission is a documented call to the Errand API using the Errand API key to check account capabilities before spending prepaid balance; this is expected for the service, not hidden exfiltration.
[SQP-3] expected: The Korean-language requirement is explained as worker-facing phone text for Seoul-based workers; it is a product/localization constraint rather than an agent takeover or security concern.
